statuses.OPEN: The published terms allow the intended use without asking anyone; conditions, if any, are listed and followed.
statuses.RESTRICTED: The published terms do not allow the intended use without permission. Not used anywhere in the project.
statuses.UNVERIFIED: Terms not found or not read. Not used anywhere until verified.

verification_levels.extraction: answer to a query about the page; quotes may be incomplete

terms_change_without_notice: All verified sites reserve the right to change terms without notice. Each entry keeps its verification date; R2 adds a hash of the terms text and re-checks before the comparator composition is recorded.

terms_hash_method.definition: The fingerprint covers the terms excerpts listed in docs/90, not byte-identical HTML (the fetch tool returns extracted text, so a byte hash would not be reproducible). Normalisation: Unicode NFC; every whitespace run -> one ASCII space; strip; join the passages with a single newline in the listed order; sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes.
terms_hash_method.recheck_rule: A mismatch means the terms changed: a new dated register entry (or a dated note) and a new audit are required before the next evaluation; history is never rewritten.

entries.basis: Series labelled 'Public Domain: Citation Requested' may be used without permission and copyrighted series with 'Citation Required' may be used with attribution, provided no prohibited use. General terms allow personal non-commercial use (view, download, print) and prohibit machine learning/AI use in a section that applies to all use, including non-commercial. Storing, caching or archiving content and wholesale downloading are prohibited in the API addendum on /legal/; the separate API terms page does not repeat them. A qualified prohibition covers robots or scraping that are disruptive. The series section and the Property Rights paragraph conflict for publication; the register follows the series labels and records the uncertainty. 2026-11-12: the channel is automation (tools/fetch_data.py): latest files from the public FRED CSV endpoint, vintage sets from the ALFRED download-data form, 147 planned quarter-end dates per series, one GET plus up to four POSTs per series per refresh (about 30 requests per run), 2 s rate limit, project User-Agent, private CI artifact retained 90 days; no FRED API key, no API cache, no catalogue crawl. Residual risk: the FAQ says 'Don't do any data mining, scraping or extraction of FRED data' without a qualifier, while the full terms qualify the robot/scraping prohibition by disruption; the owner accepted the automated channel on 2026-11-11 (D-132) and the register records the risk instead of resolving it.
conditions: CHANNEL: vintage files are retrieved automatically by the project tool (tools/fetch_data.py) on the project CI, one series per request, rate-limited, with a project User-Agent; personal non-commercial use; no human download step; no FRED API key or API cache, no bulk or wholesale download, no crawling of the catalogue; the qualified robot prohibition covers only disruptive or bulk gathering

RETRIEVAL RISK: the dense vintage retrieval (module-level batches of up to 40 dated columns, about 147 planned dates per series) is accepted on the owner reading that the qualified robot/scraping prohibition and personal non-commercial use cover a rate-limited single-series retrieval; the unqualified FAQ sentence 'Don't do any data mining, scraping or extraction of FRED data' is recorded as an open risk, not as settled permission
STORAGE: downloaded files stay in the ignored data directory; nothing from FRED or ALFRED is committed or published
ML: no training or fine-tuning of any model on FRED or ALFRED content; classical statistical estimation on the downloaded series is the intended use
ATTRIBUTION: cite FRED and the original source of each series
PUBLICATION: only derived statistics are published; the conflict in the terms is an acknowledged uncertainty, not a settled permission

SCOPE: only series listed in this register; every other series is UNVERIFIED until its label is read

entries.basis: 'The content provided on this website may be used for informational, educational, and research purposes only.' Copyrighted third-party material needs the owner's permission; names and logos may not be used as an endorsement. Research is named literally; the publication of derived statistics is not mentioned. The SPF documentation and data-sources PDF carry no separate terms section. SPF publishes CPI inflation only as quarter-over-quarter annualised and Q4/Q4 annual values (no monthly y/y), five quarterly and one or two annual horizons, with survey deadlines in the middle month of the quarter; RTDSM vintages are real GDP from 1965:Q4, CPI 1994:Q3 (quarterly) and 1998:M11 (monthly). The historical Moody's Aaa/Baa rows are provided to panelists only and are never used. 2026-11-12: tools/fetch_spf.py retrieves the public median workbooks automatically; the values are written only to the git-ignored data directory (data/raw/spf/spf_median.json) and the committed protocols/spf_metadata.json carries URLs, workbook names, sheet headers, columns used, byte sizes, SHA-256, row counts and date ranges only; raw_files_committed is false.
